title: Newton's Laws of Motion

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Laws of Motion

summary: Newton's three laws describe how forces affect motion: an object resists changes to its motion (first law), force equals mass times acceleration (second law), and every force has an equal and opposite reaction force (third law).
explanation: The first law (inertia) states that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion at constant velocity, unless acted on by a net external force — it defines what a force actually does (change motion) rather than what causes motion to continue. The second law quantifies this: net force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma), or more generally, the rate of change of momentum. The third law states that forces always come in pairs: if object A exerts a force on object B, object B exerts an equal and opposite force on object A — crucially, these two forces act on different objects, so they never cancel each other out for a single object's motion.
commonMisconceptions: Thinking a constant force is needed to maintain constant velocity — in the absence of friction/resistance, no force is needed at all (first law).
Believing action-reaction pairs act on the same object and therefore cancel — they act on two different objects and never cancel for either one individually.
examples: A book resting on a table: the table's normal force balances gravity, but the action-reaction pair for gravity is Earth pulling the book and the book pulling Earth — not the table's normal force.
genZNote: Law 1: things are lazy. Law 2: push harder, accelerate more (unless it's heavy). Law 3: the universe always sends a reply.
